tools.name: get_current_user
tools.description: Get the Tray.io account the access token belongs to (who am I)

tools.name: get_viewer
tools.description: Get the Tray.io viewer (the GraphQL identity behind the token) with its name and email

tools.name: list_workflows
tools.description: List Tray.io workflows visible to the token (id, title, enabled state, creation time)

body.query: query ($first: Int) { viewer { workflows (first: $first) { edges { node { id title enabled created } } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } } }

tools.name: list_solutions
tools.description: List Tray.io solutions (the reusable templates customer instances are created from)

body.query: query ($first: Int) { viewer { solutions (first: $first) { edges { node { id title description created } } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } } }

tools.name: list_solution_instances
tools.description: List Tray.io solution instances (per-customer deployments of a solution) with their enabled state

limit.description: Max solution instances to return (default 25, max 100)

body.query: query ($first: Int) { viewer { solutionInstances (first: $first) { edges { node { id name enabled created solution { id title } } } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } } }

tools.name: list_authentications
tools.description: List the Tray.io authentications (stored third-party service credentials) the token can see, by service

body.query: query ($first: Int) { viewer { authentications (first: $first) { edges { node { id name service { id name } } } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } } }

needs_review: THE GRAPHQL PATH IN THE BRIEF IS WRONG AND IS NOT USED HERE. Probed 2026-09-12 with a dummy bearer, `POST https://api.tray.io/core/v1/graphql` answers `404 {"message":""}`, byte-identical to the harness control path `GET https://api.tray.io/quox-shapeproof-control-abc123` -> `404 {"message":""}`, so that route does not exist. `POST https://api.tray.io/graphql` answers `200 {"data":null,"errors":[{"message":"Missing or invalid Authorization header, or user not found","extensions":{"name":"PreconditionError","code":"access_not_allowed","data":null,"isUserFacing":true,"internal":{"origin":"api-service","javaException":null,"queryContext":null}}}]}`. Every GraphQL tool therefore posts to `/graphql`.

Auth kept as scaffolded (bearer on `access_token`): the GraphQL endpoint and the REST endpoint reject the dummy bearer with the SAME message text (`Missing or invalid Authorization header, or user not found`), so one auth layer fronts both surfaces.

The GraphQL DOCUMENTS ARE NOT PROVEN AND CANNOT BE PROVEN BLIND. Tray authenticates before it parses: a deliberately broken query (`{ `), an unknown root field (`{ quoxNonexistentField }`) and an introspection query (`{ __schema { queryType { name } } }`) all return the identical PreconditionError above, never a parse or validation error. Field names and the Relay `edges { node }` / `pageInfo` connection shape come from Tray's Embedded API reference, not from a live 2xx. Introspection is unreachable and no OpenAPI or schema document is served (`/graphql` via GET, `/core/v1/openapi`, `/core/v1/swagger.json`, `/openapi.json`, `/core/v1/docs` all `404 {"message":""}`). Confirm every query against a real token before promoting this draft.

HOW THE SHAPE-PROOF MUST BE READ FOR THIS SPEC: the GraphQL tools come back HTTP 200, so the harness classifies them SHAPE_PROVEN with flags `no_auth_required` and `public_endpoint`. Both flags are about the HTTP STATUS ONLY and are misleading here: the body is an authentication refusal carried at 200, which is normal GraphQL transport. What those rows prove is one endpoint (host, TLS, path `/graphql`, JSON handling) reached six times, nothing about auth and nothing about the queries. The single row that proves the auth wiring is `test` on `/core/v1/users/me`, which answers `401 {"message":"Missing or invalid Authorization header, or user not found","details":null}` against a control `404`.

Caller input never reaches the query text. Each tool sends a FIXED read document and passes `first` through the GraphQL `variables` object, where declarativeRuntime.renderBody preserves a solo placeholder's numeric type. Interpolating `{{input.*}}` into the query string would let a caller close the read query and append a mutation, which would defeat the read-only intent of this spec (every tool is `write: false`).

GraphQL returns 200 with an `errors` array for query-level failures, so every GraphQL tool picks `errors` through. Without it a permission or schema error would be shaped into an empty result set and read as 'no workflows', a silent-fallback falsehood.

`pick` keys carry the full response path (`data.viewer.workflows.edges[]`) because applyPick sources an array from its KEY, not its value, so the output key reads `data.viewer.workflows.edges`. Functional but ugly; a spec v2 with a `from` on array picks would fix it. The same limit means one request per tool: `end_cursor` is returned but there is no next-page tool to spend it on, and `first` clamps at 100.

`get_current_user` is the one REST tool, on the only Tray REST route family that exists under a dummy key. Route mapping probed 2026-09-12: `/core/v1/users/me`, `/core/v1/users`, `/core/v1/users/{id}` and `/core/v1/workspaces` all answer `401 {"message":"Missing or invalid Authorization header, or user not found","details":null}`; `/core/v1/authentications` and `/core/v1/connectors` answer `401 {"message":"The request is unauthorized"}` (a different service behind the same gate); `/core/v1/workflows`, `/core/v1/solutions`, `/core/v1/solution-instances`, `/core/v1/logs`, `/core/v1/organizations`, `/core/v1/projects`, `/core/v1/teams` and `/core/v1/webhooks` all answer `404 {"message":""}`. So there is no REST workflow surface to read: workflows are GraphQL-only.

`get_current_user`'s picked fields (`id`, `name`, `email`, `created`) are documentation-derived like the GraphQL ones: the 401 proves the route and the auth header, never a body. The REST list routes that do exist (`/core/v1/users`, `/core/v1/workspaces`) were left out because their pagination wrapper could not be pinned down blind and a wrong wrapper would report an empty tenant.
Category changed from the scaffolded `productivity`, which is outside the 12-value taxonomy, to `developer`, matching the shipped Workato spec (the closest peer: enterprise integration platform).
